blocks.raw:
<LawCallout code="bp344" section="Section 12 - Signage">


You close your eyes in the lobby of a government hospital. You are blind and have just arrived for the first time. The receptionist has stepped away. How do you find the accessible toilet? How do you know which elevator is accessible? How do you read the evacuation plan? How do you know which dressing room has accessible features? If the building's signage package was designed correctly under BP 344, you could answer every one of these questions without opening your eyes or asking for help. If it wasn't, you're stranded. This module is the difference between those two outcomes.


</LawCallout>

### 🚨 TRAP LEART #1: Pantone 279 = "UN Blue" — Not Just "Blue"
The exam will not accept generic "blue." The answer is **Pantone 279** or **UN Blue**. If the exam shows color chips, Pantone 279 is a medium royal blue — not navy, not sky blue, not cerulean.

</Callout>

### 🚨 TRAP LEART #2: 1500 mm vs. 1800 mm for ISA at Dressing Rooms
General sign center: **1500 mm** AFF
Dressing room ISA center: **1800 mm** AFF (Sec. 13.4)
This is a deliberate exception. The higher position makes the dressing room ISA visible across a retail floor. The exam tests this difference directly.

</Callout>

<Callout variant="lea-watch" title="Trap Leart">

### 🚨 TRAP LEART #3: 2200 mm vs. 2400 mm Overhead Clearance
Projecting signs: **2200 mm** minimum vertical clearance
ATM/kiosk signage height: max **2400 mm** AFF
Both involve overhead space, but 2200 mm is a safety floor; 2400 mm is a reach-range ceiling for ATM instructional signage. These are different concepts: **safety clearance** vs. **readable height cap**.

</Callout>

### 🚨 TRAP LEART #4: Door Signs are 200 × 200 mm MINIMUM
This is frequently confused with the ISA pole sign (600 × 600 mm). Door identification plates are **smaller** — min 200 × 200 mm. The pole-mounted ISA is **larger** — 600 × 600 mm.

</Callout>

<Callout variant="lea-watch" title="Trap Leart">

### 🚨 TRAP LEART #5: Braille Grade 2, NOT Grade 1
Grade 1 = letter-for-letter (uncontracted). Grade 2 = contracted (standard literacy). **Grade 2 is the exam answer.** Grade 1 is incorrect.

</Callout>

### 🚨 TRAP LEART #7: Tactile Map Letter Height vs. Door Sign Size
Tactile map letters: **50 mm** tall (raised)
Door signs: **200 × 200 mm** plate minimum
Pictogram border: **150 mm** (on tactile maps)
These three numbers are distinct and all testable.

</Callout>

### 🚨 TRAP LEART #8: Glass Door Markings Location
Frameless full-height glass doors require markings between **900 mm and 1500 mm** AFF — this is a **range** (not just "1500 mm"). Both limits matter: lower limit prevents floor-level confusion; upper limit ensures visibility at eye level.

</Callout>
